thread:
eve_customer: hey team — after upgrading to @redwood-js/sdk v2.3.0 our Next/Vite build works but runtime requests to the hosted API get 401s only when the bundle is produced. local dev (unbundled) is fine. repro below, any ideas?

maria_support: can you paste the minimal repro and package.json? also which bundler + node version?

eve_customer: repro steps:
1) next + vite (vite-plugin-ssr)
2) npm i @redwood-js/sdk@2.3.0
3) build: npx vite build && next start
4) requests to /api/generate return 401 repeated, token present in env on server.

patrick_sdk: ugh, thanks. quick Q: are you bundling node_modules? Vite often rolls ESM and deep-imports. We had a change in 2.3.0 that moves some entrypoints and added a conditional exports map.

eve_customer: yes node_modules are bundled (server-side bundle), rollup under the hood. node 18.16.0.

jonah_eng: can you share package.json exports and TS config if present? sometimes "types" field + exports map confuses bundlers and they pick the lite ESM build without the auth shim.

eve_customer: package.json snippet:
```json
{
  "name": "app",
  "dependencies": {
    "@redwood-js/sdk": "2.3.0"
  },
  "type": "module"
}
```

maria_support: thx. can you run `node -e "console.log(require('@redwood-js/sdk/package.json').exports)"` on the runtime container? might show which subpath got resolved after bundling.

ci_bot: build-job-4721: artifact uploaded, logs at https://ci.example/4721/logs

eve_customer: ran it, output shows `{"./node": "./dist/node/index.js", "./browser": "./dist/browser/index.mjs", "./package.json": "./package.json"}` — looks like it picked ./browser entry in the bundle at runtime, which lacks server auth shim.

patrick_sdk: bingo. that explains 401. bundler substituted the browser ESM entry for server runtime during build. we added the browser field to exports in 2.3.0 which can trip bundlers that tree-shake by environment.

jonah_eng: short-term workaround: pin to 2.2.1 or override resolution to force the node entry. in Vite you can add optimizeDeps.exclude or use `alias` to point `@redwood-js/sdk` -> `@redwood-js/sdk/dist/node/index.js`

patrick_sdk: example alias for vite config:
```js
// vite.config.js
export default {
  resolve: {
    alias: {
      '@redwood-js/sdk': require('path').resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood-js/sdk/dist/node/index.js')
    }
  }
}
```

maria_support: also for Next SSR builds, ensure the server bundle is built with `external` for node_modules or use `ssr.noExternal` appropriately.

eve_customer: thanks — tried alias and it fixed the 401s. are you going to change the packaging so bundlers don't pick browser by default?

patrick_sdk: yes, we've opened ENG-1456 to rework the exports map and add clearer `node` conditional and a fallback. also plan to publish a patch 2.3.1 that reverts the ambig behavior.

jonah_eng: we'll also add a note in the changelog and a troubleshooting snippet for Vite/Next bundling.

maria_support: marking this as escalated to eng, moving to "in progress". tagging the customer with the workaround. :white_check_mark:

eve_customer: appreciated — I'll keep pinned to 2.2.1 until patch. thanks all! :)
